title: Payment Arrangements Policy — Account Eligibility, Broken-Plan Cooling-Off and Broken-Plan Limit
content:
This part of the Payment Arrangements eligibility and terms policy decides whether a placed account may take a new plan of a given type at all. Each condition is read from Ridgeline's own records for the placed account the plan would pay, as they stand before the plan is set up.

## 1. Account status

A plan is set up only on a placed account whose status is validation period or active; an account still awaiting its validation notice, in dispute hold or hardship hold, already arranged or closed takes no new plan.

| Placed account status | New plan |
|---|---|
| Validation period | May be set up (other conditions permitting) |
| Active | May be set up (other conditions permitting) |
| Awaiting its validation notice | No new plan |
| Dispute hold | No new plan |
| Hardship hold | No new plan |
| Arranged | No new plan |
| Closed | No new plan |

## 2. Stage and entry gate

The plan type must list the account's placement stage among its eligible placement stages, and the account's balance due must fall within the type's entry gate. Both are product figures of the type.

## 3. Broken-plan cooling-off

A new plan of a type is set up only when the handling date is later than the cooling-off period counted from the closing date of the most recent plan on the same account that was cancelled as broken and not reinstated. The cooling-off period is the new type's cooling-off figure in calendar days, the day after that closing date being day one.

- The clock starts from the closing date recorded on that broken plan, not from the date the plan broke or from any statement by the consumer.
- The period is counted in calendar days; its last day is still inside the period, so the handling date must fall after that last day.
- It is the cooling-off figure of the type now being set up that applies, not that of the broken plan.

**Boundary cases (hypothetical dates).** The most recent plan on the account cancelled as broken and not reinstated closed on 10 March, and the new type's cooling-off figure is 30 days. Day one is 11 March and day 30 is 9 April. A handling date of 9 April is not later than the period: the type is not set up. A handling date of 10 April is later than the period: this condition is met.

## 4. Broken-plan limit

When the number of plans on the same placed account cancelled as broken and not reinstated, counted by their closing dates over the rolling 365 calendar days ending on the handling date with both ends included, has reached the type's broken-plan limit, that type is no longer offered on the account.

**Hypothetical case.** Two plans on an account were cancelled as broken within the last 365 days. A type whose limit is 2 is no longer offered on that account; a type whose limit is 3 is not closed by this count.
